parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Use the answer to (a)(i) to show that the SI base units of pressure are $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: A horizontal pipe has length $L$ and a circular cross-section of radius $R$. A liquid of density $\rho$ flows through the pipe. The mass $m$ of liquid flowing through the pipe in time $t$ is given by $$m = \frac{\pi(p_2-p_1)R^4\rho t}{8kL}$$ where $p_1$ and $p_2$ are the pressures at the ends of the pipe and $k$ is a constant. Determine the SI base units of $k$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: An experiment is performed to determine the value of $k$ by measuring the values of the other quantities in the equation in (b). The values of $L$ and $R$ each have a percentage uncertainty of 2%. State and explain, quantitatively, which of these two quantities contributes more to the percentage uncertainty in the calculated value of $k$.

marking_points.text: units of $k = (kg\,m^{-1}\,s^{-2} \times m^4 \times kg\,m^{-3} \times s) / (kg \times m)$
$R$ contributes more to the percentage uncertainty, as $R$ is raised to the power 4 so percentage uncertainty due to $R$ is $4 \times 2\% = 8\%$, whereas due to $L$ is $2\%$
